headline: NZ fixed mortgage rates rising ahead of OCR hike as wholesale markets price in tightening cycle
reasoning: Adam Clarke explains that fixed mortgage rates are driven by wholesale market expectations of future OCR movements, not the OCR itself. Banks are already lifting fixed rates because short-term wholesale rates are spiking, signalling the market expects a rate hiking cycle to begin. However, he does not expect increases to be as dramatic as the previous cycle because the starting base is much higher and cost-of-living pressures are already constraining household spending.
quote: Fixed rates are more based around the wholesale market's expectation of the OCR in the future. And that's the real disconnect between the two.
episode_title: The mortgage traps costing Kiwis thousands

headline: Clarke expects NZ rate hiking cycle to be shallower than previous cycle due to cost-of-living constraints already squeezing households
reasoning: Clarke argues the current environment is fundamentally different from the previous hiking cycle, which came off the back of the loosest monetary policy NZ had ever seen. Because households are already under significant cost-of-living pressure, even modest rate increases should quickly dampen inflation without requiring the extreme hikes seen previously. The one-year rate bottomed around 4.45% this cycle versus 1.99% previously, meaning consumers are not coming from a position of excess cash.
quote: The previous hiking cycle came off the back end of the loosest monetary policy this country has ever seen... we're not coming off a super low base. People aren't feeling flush with cash.
episode_title: The mortgage traps costing Kiwis thousands

headline: AI-driven financial agents expected to identify and act on KiwiSaver fund misalignment, reducing consumer inertia in fund selection
reasoning: Daniel highlights that many New Zealanders are in suboptimal KiwiSaver funds (e.g. a 35-year-old in a conservative fund) and that AI agents will be able to identify misalignment daily, recommend better-performing alternatives, and facilitate switching. The agent would also consider personal context such as first-home purchase intent before making recommendations.
quote: It might be that someone who's 35 is in a conservative KiwiSaver fund and AI is going to figure that out quick, smart figure out where they would be better placed and then find the best performing one over the last 10 years and say, how about this?
episode_title: AI is coming for your finances. Are you ready?

headline: Recent major AI-fintech partnerships — Perplexity/Plaid, OpenAI/Herro acquisition, Revolut AIR — signal rapid convergence of AI chatbots and personal financial management
reasoning: Within a 10-day window, Perplexity partnered with Plaid to allow users to chat with their financial data, OpenAI acquired AI financial planning app Herro, and Revolut launched its AIR AI service in the UK offering insights and actions embedded in the neo-bank. Daniel notes over 75% of Perplexity's paying users ask a personal finance question monthly, indicating strong consumer demand driving these investments.
quote: In the last couple of weeks, there have been some really big announcements... an AI service called Perplexity has announced a product partnership with an open bank intermediary called Plaid... OpenAI has announced an acquisition of a product called Herro... Revolut have released what they call AIR, which is an AI service embedded within Revolut.
episode_title: AI is coming for your finances. Are you ready?

headline: AI set to revolutionise personal financial management apps, moving from insights to automated financial actions
reasoning: Josh Daniel argues that personal finance apps are evolving from account aggregation and spend analysis toward AI-driven agents that can take actions on behalf of users — cancelling subscriptions, optimising deposits, switching KiwiSaver funds, and filling out sign-up forms. He sees AI reducing financial inertia as the core disruption, with major announcements from Perplexity, OpenAI (Herro acquisition), and Revolut's AIR product signalling the direction of travel.
quote: What the AI will be able to do is cut through all the marketing nonsense and just look at what is actually the best financial product for you and for nearly everyone that will not be your current financial products.
episode_title: AI is coming for your finances. Are you ready?

headline: AI agents threaten to disintermediate mortgage brokers and insurance advisors as digital platforms take over routine financial advice tasks
reasoning: Daniel identifies that two of the three main reasons clients use mortgage advisors — securing the best rate and handling administrative paperwork — can be fully automated digitally. Only the desire for human sparring and advice remains sticky, and even that may erode over time. New Zealand digital platforms like Homely and AnteUp are already offering end-to-end digital home loan services without human client relationships.
quote: Both those two jobs can be done digitally. They don't need a human to do it.
episode_title: AI is coming for your finances. Are you ready?

headline: Removal of human intermediaries in insurance and financial product distribution should structurally lower costs for consumers, but competitive disruption rather than gradual margin pass-through is the likely mechanism
reasoning: Daniel argues that incumbent financial product providers will not voluntarily pass commission savings to consumers once brokers are removed; instead, a new entrant willing to operate on lower margins will force competitive repricing. The equilibrium will shift via competitive disruption rather than gradual reform.
quote: My prediction would be, you won't see this gradual trickle through of the economics of the consumer. It will be more like the landscape stays as it is until a competitor comes and shows a new way and everyone has to react to that competitive force.
episode_title: AI is coming for your finances. Are you ready?
